title: 2026 National Resilience Strategy
summary: The National Resilience Strategy defines resilience as a strategic capability and applies risk prioritization, modernization, distributed responsibility, and simplified governance across national security, the economy, public health and safety, and infrastructure reliability. It places states, local governments, industry, and citizens inside the operating model.
key_findings: The strategy favors risk-informed investment and modernization over a uniform all-hazards approach.
Infrastructure reliability and continuity of essential services are core resilience domains.
Responsibility is distributed across federal, state, local, private, and individual actors.
why_it_matters: It provides a national framework for the receiving systems where technology, infrastructure, and policy meet local authority and operational responsibility.
ftfn_relevance: Supports local-system analysis and clearer allocation of authority.
Adds a policy frame for infrastructure modernization, continuity, and risk prioritization.
evidence_limits: The strategy does not quantify risk or identify completed resilience investments.
Implementation will depend on later doctrine, budgets, agency actions, and state or local records.
